expected_evidence: geological: synchronous stratigraphic markers at the ~12,900 cal BP boundary across multiple continents (Younger Dryas Boundary 'black mat' layers, elevated platinum/iridium concentrations, nanodiamonds, magnetic microspherules, soot/charcoal spikes) interpreted as a cosmic-impact or airburst signature

astronomical: orbital-dynamics modeling showing Earth intersecting a dense filament of the Taurid meteor/comet stream (debris from a hypothesized fragmenting giant comet) at ~10,950 BCE, and/or radiant/fireball corridor reconstructions consistent with a multi-fragment encounter

geological: abrupt proxy shifts (ice-core dust/ammonium spikes, lake-sediment cooling signals, pollen reversal) at sites in North America, Europe, and the Middle East dated tightly to the same centuries, used to argue synchroneity of onset
material: disruption or abandonment horizons in Late Paleolithic/Clovis-era archaeological layers coincident with the boundary layer (e.g., reduced site density, tool-tradition discontinuities)
genetic: megafaunal extinction/bottleneck signatures in ancient DNA dated close to the proposed event horizon
oral_tradition/iconographic: purported 'sky-fire' or catastrophe motifs in later mythologies retrojected onto this event (low-confidence, largely model-prior speculation, not primary evidence)

model_prior: the broader 'Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis' and its association with the Taurid complex as discussed in the geoscience literature (Firestone et al., Napier, Bailey, and subsequent critiques) — this is recalled from training rather than from supplied evidence text, so it should be treated as unverified model-prior, not established fact
response.rationale: The hypothesis sits right at the Pleistocene/Younger Dryas transition (~10,950 BCE), so the relevant detectability profile is best approximated by the 'younger-dryas' row rather than later periods: textual (0.0) and linguistic (0.05) evidence are essentially impossible this far back, and oral_tradition/iconographic (0.1) are only weakly preservable and easily distorted over ~13,000 years, so their absence carries little evidentiary weight against the hypothesis. However, the two evidence kinds most directly implicated by this hypothesis — astronomical (orbital modeling of the Taurid stream) and geological (boundary-layer proxies like platinum anomalies, nanodiamonds, black mats) — have comparatively high detectability (0.7 and 0.65) for this period, since geological stratigraphy from ~11 ka is routinely preserved and datable, and astronomical/orbital reconstructions are computable independent of physical relics. Material and genetic evidence (0.35, 0.3) are moderately detectable but easily confounded with normal climatic/ecological signals of the era. Given that the strongest expected evidence types for this specific mechanism happen to be the more detectable ones, an absence of confirmed multi-continent synchronous impact markers is more evidentially meaningful here than it would be for, say, a purely textual claim — yet the genuine ambiguity/contestation of existing YDB-layer data (platinum/nanodiamond findings are real but their impact-origin interpretation is disputed by mainstream geoscience) means the evidence base is real but equivocal, not simply absent due to poor preservation. I set a composite detectability_adjustment of 0.5, averaging the high astronomical/geological plausibility against the weaker material/genetic/oral_tradition channels and the acknowledgment that any 'confirmation' language ('corroborated') overstates the actual contested state of the geological record. The Taurid-mechanism specifics and the 'corroborated' framing draw heavily on model-prior recollection of the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis literature, which remains a minority/contested position in geoscience — this should be flagged as low-tier model-prior rather than settled fact.
